title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is working in a model structure on A^ (presheaves on a small category A, probably a test category). The weak equivalences W are those of the localizer, and 'W-Kan objects' are the fibrant objects. The page is part of a proof that some comparison map (*) involving a sequential colimit X_0 ↪ X_1 ↪ X_2 ↪ ... is bijective.

(1) Reduction. One may assume Y is a W-Kan (fibrant) object. Then Hom_Hot(X,Y) is the set of homotopy classes of maps X→Y. Moreover, for such Y the homotopy relation (the equivalence relation generated by elementary homotopies through a cylinder or interval) already coincides with elementary homotopy. This is the analogue of the fact that for a Kan complex, Δ^1-homotopy is already an equivalence relation.

(2) The rectification problem. We have maps g_n: X_n → Y with g_{n+1} f_n ≃ g_n, where the f_n are cofibrations (monomorphisms). We want g'_n ≃ g_n with g'_{n+1} f_n = g'_n strictly. Such a family induces a map colim X_n → Y. So this is the statement that a compatible family of homotopy classes lifts to a strictly compatible family of maps. In Milnor-sequence terms, that gives surjectivity of [colim X_n, Y] → lim [X_n, Y]. Injectivity of that map is controlled by lim^1, so the label 'injectivity of (*)' suggests (*) runs in the other direction or is a different map; the problem actually treated here is a lifting/strictification.

(3) Generalisation. Take a square with i: X → X' a cofibration, p: Y → Y' a fibration, top map g, bottom map g', and a diagonal φ: X' → Y such that both triangles commute only up to homotopy:
- φ i ≃ g via a homotopy k;
- p φ ≃ g' via a homotopy h.
Assume X, X' cofibrant and Y, Y' fibrant, so that left and right homotopy agree (Quillen). Question: is there φ̄ ≃ φ making both triangles commute strictly?
- Grothendieck identifies this with Quillen's 'covering homotopy extension theorem' for simplicial closed model categories (Homotopical Algebra, Ch. II §2), complaining that Quillen's formulation was hard to make sense of.
- The marginal note gives the right criterion. The two resulting homotopies from pφi to g'i = pg, namely p∘k and h∘i, must be homotopic as homotopies (a homotopy between homotopies). In modern terms, (φ, k, h) is a point of the homotopy pullback Map(X,Y) ×^h_{Map(X,Y')} Map(X',Y'). The pullback-corner map Map(X',Y) → Map(X,Y) ×_{Map(X,Y')} Map(X',Y') is a Kan fibration (SM7). Hence φ can be strictified within its homotopy class exactly when this 2-cell coherence condition holds; otherwise there is an obstruction in π_1 of Map(X,Y').

(4) Back to the special case Y' = e. There the coherence condition is vacuous, and the problem reduces to the homotopy extension property of the cofibration f_n into the fibrant Y. So the induction g'_{n+1} := homotopy-extended g_{n+1} works.
errors: The heading 'Injectivity of (*)' does not match the problem actually treated. Strictifying a homotopy-compatible family g_n to a strictly compatible one is a surjectivity statement for [colim X_n, Y] → lim [X_n, Y]. Injectivity of that map fails in general, with obstruction lim^1. Either (*) denotes a map in the opposite direction or the label is loose; the definition of (*) is on an earlier page.

In the general square, homotopy-commutativity of the two triangles alone is not sufficient. One needs the compatibility of p∘k and h∘i as homotopies. Grothendieck notices this himself in the margin ('This is presumably sufficient!'). The condition is indeed sufficient for cofibration/fibration with cofibrant/fibrant objects, and necessary in the appropriate sense.

ideas.what: For a fibrant (Kan) object Y, the homotopy relation on maps X→Y equals elementary (one-step) homotopy, and Hom_Hot(X,Y) is the set of homotopy classes
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy relation for maps into fibrant objects; left/right homotopy coincidence
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (discussions of elementary homotopies and homotopy intervals)

ideas.what: Strictifying a homotopy-compatible sequence of maps X_n → Y out of a sequence of cofibrations, via homotopy extension
ideas.modern_name: Rectification via homotopy extension property; Milnor lim/lim^1 sequence for [colim X_n, Y]

ideas.what: A diagonal in a cofibration/fibration square that commutes up to homotopy can be replaced by a homotopic diagonal making it strictly commute, iff the two induced homotopies pφi ⇒ g'i are homotopic
ideas.modern_name: Covering homotopy extension theorem; SM7 pullback-corner fibration; strict vs homotopy pullback of mapping spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen, Homotopical Algebra (1967), Ch. II §2; classical CHEP (Strøm et al.)

missed.claim: The scrap paper (a CNUSC job log dated Friday 4 June 1982 on the preceding sheet) gives a terminus post quem for these closed-model notes. They predate Pursuing Stacks (begun Feb. 1983), which refines the archive's 'à partir de 1982'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor dating evidence for when Grothendieck engaged with Quillen's Homotopical Algebra before Pursuing Stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard model-category homotopy theory: homotopy extension, rectification and Quillen's covering homotopy extension. The only mild interest is Grothendieck's reaction to Quillen's formulation and his correct identification of the 2-cell coherence condition.
transcription_corrections: Margin note likely reads 'There is such a possibility, iff (?) we can find k and h s.th. the two resulting homotopies pφi → g'i and pφi → pg ... are homotopic' — the comparison is between p∘k and h∘i as homotopies from pφi to g'i = pg.
The parenthesis should read roughly '(we assume X, X' cofibrant, Y, Y' fibrant, so that ~ and ≈ are the same in any model category)', i.e. left and right homotopy coincide.
Diagram: maps g_n: X_n → Y with f_n: X_n → X_{n+1}; in the next sentence 'where i: X→X' is f_n' and 'p: Y→Y' is the map Y→e'.
The final reference is to Quillen's Homotopical Algebra, Ch. II, §2, Prop. 4 (as written, 'prop. 4 of Ch. II no 2.4' / '§2').
